title: Inference degradation causal waterfall and observability contract
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
Build a causal "waterfall" view and an accompanying observability contract to reliably attribute inference degradations (timeouts, overloads, model failures, HTTP/gRPC errors) to the correct service phase (edge/gateway, router, runtime, model, postprocess). This ticket covers instrumentation spec, trace/span semantics, log/metric schema v2, dashboard panels, alert tuning, and a staged rollout plan.

Background/Rationale:
Operators currently struggle to determine whether a high-p99 latency or error spike is caused by upstream network overload, request routing hotpaths, model stalls (KV cache cold-paths), or model-internal exceptions (nan/oom). Investigations are time-consuming because traces lack consistent phase tags, logs are hard to join to spans, and dashboards aggregate error codes without causal context.

Goals:
- Define an observability contract (span names, attributes, error tags) consumed by runtime, gateway, and router so UIs can produce a causal waterfall view per request.
- Extend metrics/log pipeline to emit phase-level latency/error time series and a normalized failure taxonomy (timeout, overload, model_error, protocol_error, internal).
- Implement dashboard widgets: "Phase waterfall" (latency and error attribution stacked by phase), "Error slice" (by HTTP/gRPC code, model variant, route), and a drilldown link to sampled full traces.
- Add alerting rules that map SLO breaches to most-likely phase with confidence score.

Non-Goals:
- Rewriting existing long-term storage. We will add tags and new time series; retention and storage tier changes are separate tickets.

Acceptance criteria (see list below) and query examples included in attachments.
acceptance_criteria: Observability contract doc checked into Confluence with span names, required attributes, and error taxonomy mapping (timeout, overload, model_error, protocol_error, internal).
Runtime/gateway/ingress libraries updated to emit phase attribute (phase=ingest|route|runtime|model|post|cache) and failure_type attribute when errors occur.
Metrics pipeline emits phase.latency.{p50,p95,p99} and phase.error_rate time series for all public routes within 48 hours of rollout.
Dashboards: Phase waterfall panel that stacks latency contribution by phase and a companion stacked error-rate breakdown by failure_type. Panels show model variant, route, and region filters.
Trace sampling: 100% of errors are kept (head-sampled) with full traces linked from dashboards; normal requests sampled to 1% by default.
Playbook: For each failure_type there is a short runbook mapping likely causes and first three diagnostic queries. Runbook linked from dashboard.
Rollout: Canary rollout to 10% of traffic in staging then 5%/25%/100% in production with observability metrics demonstrating no signal loss.
implementation_steps: Finalize observability contract (Confluence) and review with runtime/gateway/console owners (2 d).

Add span/attribute changes: - gateway: annotate spans with phase=ingest and attach upstream proto code; - router: phase=route with chosen_model and route_decision; - runtime: emit phase=runtime and KV cache hit/miss tag; - model kernel: emit phase=model with model_error details. (5 d).

Update logging enrichment pipeline: map new attributes into structured logs and set normalized failure_type field; ensure http.status and grpc.code are normalized into protocol_error when appropriate (3 d).
Metrics generation: produce phase-based latency histograms and error counters in the pipeline; add labels for model_variant, route, region (3 d).
Dashboard creation: implement waterfall and error-slice panels, with efficient backend queries and links to trace viewer (4 d).
Alerting: author rules that compute phase-level attribution for SLO breaches using majority-of-error-weight heuristic and surface confidence score (2 d).
Canary rollout and validation: staging canary -> phased prod rollout with verification dashboards and postmortem template. (5 d).
tradeoffs: Sampling fidelity vs storage cost: keeping 100% of errors increases storage and ingestion costs; mitigation is to head-sample errors and reduce retention to 30 days for full traces.
Attribute cardinality: adding model_variant and route labels improves troubleshooting but increases TSDB series cardinality; we'll limit to top N variants per project and roll up others to 'other'.
Pipeline latency vs enrichment completeness: enriching logs with heavy model metadata at emit-time adds tail latency; prefer async enrichment in pipeline where possible.
Dashboard query complexity: aggregated waterfall may be expensive; will maintain pre-aggregated phase buckets for last 24h and on-demand raw queries for longer windows.
